summary: Static code review of Apps Script fix for 'No response from server' bug. Verified sanitizeForClient_ implementation in /app/apps-script/Code.gs and its application at every RPC boundary. Runtime testing not possible (Google Apps Script on Crux Workspace SSO). All 5 review criteria from the request pass.
critical_code_review_comments: sanitizeForClient_ (Code.gs:169-180) correctly handles null, undefined->null, Date->ISO-8601 via Utilities.formatDate(v, getTz_(), "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssXXX"), function->null, Array (recursive), Object (recursive key-preserving), primitives pass through. Idempotent for already-safe input.

Applied at RPC success exit (Code.gs:145 -> {ok:true, data: sanitizeForClient_(out)}) and at bootstrap payload (Code.gs:32 -> tpl.bootstrap = JSON.stringify(sanitizeForClient_(getBootstrap_()))). Correct.
Error path (Code.gs:146-159) returns {ok:false, error:<friendly string>}. Strings are already safe; sanitising unnecessary and correctly omitted.
logAudit_ call inside the RPC catch block is wrapped in its own try/catch (Code.gs:149-158) so a Sheets write failure during audit cannot re-throw and mask the friendly error return. Correct.

Client-side google.script.run usage: only ONE occurrence in the entire client tree (App.html:28), and it always routes through the rpc() Promise wrapper. Index.html and Portal.html contain zero direct RPC calls (Portal is server-rendered). No raw Date can leak past the sanitiser.
Helper dependencies verified present: getTz_ (Utils.gs:19), nowIso_ (Utils.gs:12), safePayload_ (Utils.gs:111), AuthError_ (Utils.gs:5), logAudit_ (Sheets.gs:283).
Known limitation (documented and accepted): sanitizeForClient_ will infinite-loop on genuine circular references. Sheet-derived data has no circles, so this is safe in practice.
Minor style nit (non-blocking): Code.gs:170 `return v === undefined ? null : v;` is slightly convoluted after the outer null-or-undefined guard; equivalent to `return null;`. No functional impact.

Spot-checked RPC routes (clients.list, clients.get, dashboard.summary, admin.logs.email, ai.status, portal.getLink) — all pass through the single dispatcher, so all get sanitised uniformly. No route bypasses the wrapper.
context_for_next_testing_agent: This is a Google Apps Script project — no runtime testing possible in Emergent container. Reviews here are static only. The Date-serialisation bug fix is well-scoped and correct. If user re-reports 'No response from server' after redeploy, next step is to have them run the deployed URL, open DevTools console, and capture the actual server response object — if res is genuinely undefined, look for uncaught exceptions in Apps Script's Executions log, not in the sanitiser.
rca of the issue: google.script.run cannot serialise native JS Date objects across the client boundary; it silently returns undefined to the success handler. Rows read from Google Sheets contain Date objects for date-typed cells (Timestamp, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, ExecutedAt, EffectiveFrom, EffectiveTo). The client-side rpc() wrapper interpreted the undefined as 'No response from server'. Mitigation: sanitizeForClient_ walks the return value recursively converting Date->ISO string (Asia/Kolkata), undefined->null, function->null before returning. Applied at both the rpc() dispatcher exit and the doGet bootstrap serialisation point. Reproduction: any RPC whose Sheets read includes a date cell would previously fail on the client with 'No response from server'; after fix, returns ISO string.
